title: Vanilla Crème Pâtissière (Pastry Cream)
summary: A thick, smooth vanilla pastry cream of milk, egg yolks and cornflour, boiled briefly, finished with butter and chilled for piping or spreading.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, cut into 4 pieces

steps.title: Make the yolk base
steps.text: Whisk the yolks, 25 g of the sugar and the cornflour in the bowl for about 1 min until pale and thick. Heat the milk, salt and remaining sugar in the saucepan until it just begins to simmer.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisk half the hot milk into the yolks in a thin stream. Warming the yolks gradually stops them scrambling, then pour everything back into the pan.

steps.title: Boil the custard
steps.text: Whisk constantly over medium heat until the cream thickens and a few large bubbles burst on the surface. Keep whisking for 1 min more; this takes it well past 82 °C and cooks out the cornflour so it sets firmly instead of thinning.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Take it off the heat and whisk in the cold butter and vanilla until smooth. Push it through the sieve into the shallow dish to remove any lumps.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Press cling film onto the surface so no skin forms and chill for at least 3 h. Whisk it smooth before piping or spreading.

tips: A common mistake is stopping before the cream boils, which leaves it tasting of starch and turning runny.
Keep the whisk moving across the base of the pan, where it catches first.
A shallow dish lets the custard cool quickly and safely.
For a lighter filling, fold in some softly whipped cream just before using.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Not suitable for freezing.
